turns.prompt:
<mission>
Produce a reusable prompt that reliably does turning my rough meeting notes into a client follow-up email for freelance bookkeepers who work with small restaurants.
</mission>

<task>
1. Ask me up to five questions, one at a time, about the task,
   audience, constraints, and what a great result looks like. Stop
   asking when you have enough.
2. Write the prompt with MASTER layers. Use [brackets] for inputs.
3. Write three test inputs: typical, hard, and edge case.
4. Predict how the prompt might fail on each and revise it to
   prevent that.
</task>

<eval>
The prompt has a one-sentence mission, numbered steps, at least three
checkable eval criteria, and an exact output format. No layer is empty.
</eval>

<output>
The final prompt in a code block, then the three test inputs, then a
list of assumptions you made.
</output>
turns.output: What tone should these follow-up emails use with small-restaurant clients—warm and conversational (first-name, like a trusted local partner), or more formal and professional?

message.reasoning_content:
I need to build a reusable prompt that converts rough meeting notes into client follow-up emails for freelance bookkeepers serving small restaurants.

I will ask up to five clarifying questions about the task, audience, and desired outcome. Then I will draft a MASTER-layer prompt with bracketed inputs. I will create three test cases: typical, hard, and edge case. I will predict failure modes for each and revise the prompt to prevent them. The final deliverable must include a one-sentence mission, numbered steps, at least three checkable criteria, an exact output format, and no empty layers.

I am clarifying the MASTER layer framework. I am unsure whether the acronym stands for Mission, Audience, Steps, Tone, Examples, and Result format, or a simpler structure like Mission, Audience, Steps, and Constraints.

I have settled on the MASTER layer structure: Mission, Audience, Steps, Tone, Eval criteria, and Result format. I am now drafting the first clarifying question.

I have identified six specific clarifying questions to ask. These cover tone, required content, length limits, branding, note quality, and how to handle missing information.

I am adding two more clarifying angles: whether meetings are one-on-one or involve multiple attendees, and what specific bookkeeping topics the emails should cover. I will ask one question at a time and stop once I have enough context.
